title_en: Guo Ziwen Bribery and Speculation Case

full_text_en:
Guo Ziwen Case of Acceptance of Bribes and Speculation

Appellant: Guo Ziwen, male, 52 years old, formerly General Manager of China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation. Arrested on October 10, 1993.

After trial by the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, the Court rendered judgment on June 7, 1994, in the case concerning the appellant Guo Ziwen's acceptance of bribes and speculation, holding: Guo Ziwen committed the crime of accepting bribes and was sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life and forfeiture of all personal property; he committed the crime of speculation and was sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life; the combined sentence was death, with deprivation of political rights for life and forfeiture of all personal property. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, Guo Ziwen refused to accept it and appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. The Beijing High People's Court, upon trial, found the facts as follows:

In early 1993, China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation, subordinate to the Ministry of Coal Industry, was established, and the appellant Guo Ziwen was appointed General Manager. Within just a few months of taking office, Guo Ziwen, taking advantage of his position, engaged in economic criminal activities in the course of providing short-term loans of public funds to relevant companies, depositing public funds, making donations and sponsorship payments, and selling the Corporation's retained foreign exchange quotas. The facts are as follows:

(1) From April to June 1993, the appellant Guo Ziwen, without proper authorization, decided to lend public funds to Zhenhai Coal Mine Machinery Equipment Supply Company of Lianyungang City, Jiangsu Province (with loan periods of one to two months) in five installments totaling RMB 34.1 million. Guo Ziwen, in his office and at his home, twice accepted bribes of RMB 10,000 and RMB 50,000 from Li Yongji (handled in a separate case), the responsible person of that company. At the time the case came to light, RMB 13 million of the public funds lent out had become overdue and remained unpaid; after recovery efforts by the judicial authorities, over RMB 4.1789 million was still unable to be recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by the confession of the briber Li Yongji; testimony of witnesses including Yang Dexuan, Guo Ping, and Li Qiang; documentary evidence including five loan contracts, bank drafts, and the property loss report of China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation; and the recovered bribe proceeds.

(2) On May 30, 1993, the appellant Guo Ziwen decided to deposit RMB 5 million of the Corporation's funds into the Dalian Office of China Venturetech Investment Corporation. On the same day, Guo Ziwen in his office accepted a bribe of RMB 50,000 given by Yang Tao, the deputy director of that office. The above facts are confirmed by testimony of the briber Yang Tao and Zhang Yonggang, who withdrew the bribe cash; documentary evidence including one trust deposit certificate; and recovered cash of RMB 50,000 bearing the seal of Dalian Industrial and Commercial Bank.

(3) Between May and June 1993, the appellant Guo Ziwen decided to deposit RMB 25 million of the Corporation's public funds into Zhongguancun City Credit Cooperative of Haidian District, Beijing, in three separate installments. Guo Ziwen in his office accepted from Wang Xuebing of that credit cooperative a six-month time deposit certificate in Wang Xuebing's name for a bribe of RMB 50,000.

The above facts are confirmed by testimony of the briber Wang Xuebing; documentary evidence including three time deposit certificates for RMB 25 million and one recovered deposit certificate for RMB 50,000.

(4) Between June and July 1993, at the request of Wu Hong, Assistant General Manager of Beijing Santiago Advertising Company, the appellant Guo Ziwen decided that the Corporation would sponsor "1993 China Corporate Culture Festival" Organizing Committee twice, totaling RMB 100,000. Guo Ziwen, in his office and at the Great Hall of the People, twice accepted bribes of RMB 8,000 from Wu Hong. On September 8 of the same year, when Wu Hong was summoned for other issues, she confessed the above facts to the procuratorial authorities and informed Guo Ziwen of her confession. Upon learning that the matter was exposed, on September 11, Guo Ziwen returned the RMB 8,000 to Wu Hong.

The above facts are confirmed by testimony of the briber Wu Hong and witness Yang Dexuan; documentary evidence including two receipts for the RMB 100,000 sponsorship, a receipt written by Wu Hong, and deposit certificates.

(5) In May 1993, Bai Hua, a business person of Beijing Ruide Industrial Corporation, through the private arrangement of Wang Qihe, a cadre of the Foreign Exchange Adjustment Center of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and with the introduction of Yuan Qibin (at large), an accountant of the Finance Department of China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation, reached an agreement with the appellant Guo Ziwen. The agreement provided that China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation would allocate to Beijing Ruide Industrial Corporation a retained foreign exchange quota of over USD 510,000. Guo Ziwen therefore demanded from Ruide Industrial Corporation a portion of cash as a "General Manager's Fund." After the Central Foreign Exchange Business Center of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange completed the procedures for transferring the USD quota, in early June of the same year, Guo Ziwen in his office accepted a bribe of RMB 100,000 forwarded by Wang Qihe from Beijing Ruide Industrial Corporation.

In July of the same year, Bai Hua again, through Wang Qihe and Yuan Qibin, reached an agreement with the appellant Guo Ziwen, providing that China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation would allocate to Beijing Ruide Industrial Corporation another retained foreign exchange quota of over RMB 1.61 million (in USD equivalent). For this, Guo Ziwen accepted at his home a bribe of RMB 200,000 forwarded by Wang Qihe.

The above facts are confirmed by testimony of the bribers Wang Qihe and Bai Hua, and witnesses Li Chunsheng, Chai Yulian, Guo Ping, Guo Jin, Guo Hong, Shen Ying, Li Jingning, Cai Ting, and Yang Dexuan; relevant documents including the foreign exchange quota payment order from the Central Foreign Exchange Business Center of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange; and documentary evidence including seized deposit certificates for the bribe amount of RMB 300,000.

In summary, the appellant Guo Ziwen, taking advantage of his position, demanded and accepted bribes from entities and individuals totaling RMB 468,000.

All the above bribe proceeds were recovered after the case came to light.

In addition, in mid-May 1993, the appellant Guo Ziwen's son-in-law Zou Yanfei (co-defendant, already sentenced) learned that Sinochem International Chemicals Co., Ltd. urgently needed to purchase USD quotas and informed Guo Ziwen. Guo Ziwen indicated that they could sell a USD 2 million retained quota at a ratio of RMB 3.2 per USD 1 of retained quota. Of this ratio, RMB 3.1 per USD (total RMB 6.2 million) was to be paid by check to China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation, and the remaining RMB 0.1 per USD (total RMB 200,000) was to be paid in cash, instructing Zou Yanfei to conduct the transaction. Zou Yanfei reached an agreement with Sinochem International Chemicals Co., Ltd. at a ratio of 3.7:1, and Guo Ziwen signed the agreement. On May 27, after the Central Foreign Exchange Business Center of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange completed the quota transfer procedures, Sinochem International Chemicals Co., Ltd. delivered to Zou Yanfei four checks totaling RMB 7.39 million payable to China Coal Sales and Transportation Corporation, along with RMB 100,000 in cash. Zou Yanfei should have deposited these funds into the Corporation's account, but instead, through Guo Ziwen's connections, transferred them into a personal account he had opened at a bank. On June 3, Zou Yanfei withdrew from his personal account a check for RMB 6.2 million and, together with RMB 200,000 in cash, totaling RMB 6.4 million, returned it to the Corporation. The remaining RMB 1.09 million was divided between Zou Yanfei and Guo Ziwen.

The above facts are confirmed by testimony of witnesses Wang Xuebing, Yu Wenxiu, and Ge Wenjun; relevant documents including the foreign exchange quota transfer order from the Central Foreign Exchange Business Center of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange; bank transfer vouchers and bank ledger records; and recovered bribe proceeds of RMB 1.09 million.

The Beijing High People's Court found: The appellant Guo Ziwen demanded and accepted bribes totaling RMB 468,000, and colluded with Zou Yanfei to privately and at an inflated price sell foreign exchange quotas for huge illegal profits of RMB 1.09 million. The facts are clear and the evidence is conclusive, sufficient to establish the offenses. Guo Ziwen, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to seek benefits for related enterprises and demanded or accepted bribes from them. His conduct constitutes the crime of accepting bribes under Article 4 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery. The amount of bribes accepted is especially huge, and the circumstances of the crime are especially serious; accordingly, he should be severely punished under Article 5, Paragraph 1, and Article 2, Item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions. Guo Ziwen, in violation of state foreign exchange control regulations, colluded with others to privately sell retained USD quotas for huge illegal profits, and the amount of illegal gains is especially huge. His conduct violates Article 118 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and constitutes the crime of speculation. The circumstances of his crime are especially serious, and as a state functionary, he should be subject to a heavier punishment under Article 1, Item (1) of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy. Guo Ziwen committed multiple crimes and should be subjected to combined punishment for multiple crimes under Article 64 of the Criminal Law. Guo Ziwen should also have his political rights deprived for life in accordance with Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. The criminal judgment of the Beijing Intermediate People's Court is correct and should be affirmed. Guo Ziwen argued on appeal that the sums of RMB 10,000 and RMB 50,000 in bribes he accepted had been turned over to the public; upon investigation, these claims were untrue and could not be sustained. He also argued that accepting the six-month deposit certificate for RMB 50,000 in the name of Wang Xueping constituted an attempted acceptance of bribes; however, since Wang Xueping had delivered this deposit certificate to Guo Ziwen for his control and disposal, and the deposit certificate was a bearer instrument payable on demand, Guo Ziwen's argument that it was "an attempted acceptance of bribes" is obviously a sophistry and is not accepted. Accordingly, on June 22, 1994, the Beijing High People's Court ruled: the appeal of the appellant Guo Ziwen is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

In accordance with Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing High People's Court submitted the criminal ruling affirming the death sentence, deprivation of political rights for life, and forfeiture of all personal property for Guo Ziwen to the Supreme People's Court for approval. The Supreme People's Court, after review in accordance with the death penalty review procedure under the Criminal Procedure Law, ruled on June 29, 1994: the criminal ruling of the Beijing High People's Court upholding the first-instance judgment sentencing the defendant Guo Ziwen to death for accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life and forfeiture of all personal property; and sentencing him to death for speculation, with deprivation of political rights for life, with the combined sentence of death, deprivation of political rights for life, and forfeiture of all personal property, is hereby approved.
